encoding: lp(...) writes each part as its byte length (4 bytes, big-endian) then its bytes. Inside lp: text (labels, ids such as c_, r_, en_, ap_ and sr_ ids, actions, targets, emails, roles) as UTF-8; integers (seq, generation, requestedAt) as decimal ASCII; hashes (previewHash, a previous rosterHash or policyHash, the first being 32 zero bytes) as their raw 32 bytes; credentialId, cose, attestationObject, clientDataJSON, spki and serials as raw bytes. canonical_json is AC-1 3.6's (CE-1 with null). In JSON: hashes and fingerprints are lowercase hex; keys, certificates, MACs, nonces and signatures are base64url without padding; serials are lowercase hex; times are milliseconds. Every ECDSA signature is the ASN.1 DER ECDSA-Sig-Value.

profile.signature: ecdsa-with-SHA384 (1.2.840.10045.4.3.3) for every certificate, by the P-384 CA key
profile.names: UTF8String attributes; CA subject [CN, O] in that order; server subject CN=<public host>; relay subject CN=<relayId>
profile.validity: UTCTime before 2050, GeneralizedTime from 2050; CA 10 years, leaves 90 days
profile.serial: 16 bytes, first byte (b & 0x7f) | 0x40, so positive with no leading zero
profile.ca: basicConstraints critical CA true pathLen 0; keyUsage critical keyCertSign cRLSign; subjectKeyIdentifier
profile.server: basicConstraints critical CA false (empty SEQUENCE); keyUsage critical digitalSignature; extendedKeyUsage serverAuth; subjectAltName DNS names
profile.relay: basicConstraints critical CA false; keyUsage critical digitalSignature; extendedKeyUsage clientAuth; subjectAltName URI urn:lucid:relay:<relayId>; subjectKeyIdentifier; authorityKeyIdentifier keyIdentifier
profile.key_identifier: the first 20 bytes of SHA-256 of the subjectPublicKey bits (the SEC1 uncompressed point), RFC 7093 method 1
profile.pin: SHA-256 of the CA certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, 64 lowercase hex; the CA fingerprint trust-ca takes is the same value

manifest.label: lucid-fleet-trust-v1
manifest.about: signing input lp(label, canonical_json(manifest without sig)); sig by the CA of caGeneration (ECDSA P-384 SHA-384, DER, base64url); stored.sha256 is SHA-256 of canonical_json of the whole stored manifest (sig included), so "equal with the same bytes" compares that digest

rollover.about: nextCa in a manifest signed by generation g is stored pending and never trusted on that signature; only trust-ca with the matching fingerprint (the pin, 64 hex, compared ignoring case and spaces) makes it active

distrust.label: lucid-fleet-distrust-v1
distrust.about: sig over lp(label, consoleId, generation) by any CA the relay pins (active or pending); a distrust only removes trust; with no active pin left the relay is read only and silent until a confirmed pin exists

trusted_time.about: 3.10 (revision 3.2): T advances only by the monotonic clock while running; wall more than 10 minutes ahead or more than 5 minutes behind makes the relay clock-uncertain. Wall only ahead: the stored manifest and the channel stay usable at T, and a pushed or fetched manifest is accepted when not older than the stored one, issuedAt no more than 5 minutes after T and T before expiresAt (wall time unused). At every start and while wall is behind, the stored manifest counts as expired and a fetched one is accepted only when not older than the stored one, issuedAt no more than 5 minutes after wall time and wall time no later than expiresAt, then T = max(T, issuedAt). trust-time reset needs a manifest from an active pinned CA with a seq strictly higher than the stored one and issuedAt within 10 minutes of wall time (it may be below the stored issuedAt), the server leaf listed and not revoked in it; the new manifest replaces the stored one and T = its issuedAt; reset checks in the order no-manifest, unpinned-ca, signature, not-higher, far, revoked, not-listed
